source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_003],
After reviewing both the datasheet and the schematic, I can confirm that pin 5 on U3 is connected incorrectly and is causing the problem.

execution.observed_behavior: Datasheet and schematic review confirmed that U3 pin 5 was connected incorrectly and that the incorrect USBLC6 wiring caused the USB failure.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: For a permanent solution that retains the ESD protection, the symbol should be corrected so pin 5 (VBUS) connects to +5V and pin 2 connects separately to GND, rather than having them tied together. The D+/D- pass-through via U3 should remain unchanged. With the USBLC6 wired properly, USB will function while the protection is restored. Is that the change you intend to make? There is no rush; I will continue testing in the meantime.

value_updates.data_line_routing: D+/D- pass-through via U3 remains unchanged
value_updates.required_outcome: USB functions with ESD protection retained

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer claims completion of the authorized USBLC6 ESD-protection wiring correction.

routing_warnings.description: The failure to enumerate or flash is direct execution evidence for native USB programming; the ESD-specific wiring cause is represented separately.
USB operation after removing U3 and bridging the data lines verifies native USB programming, not operation of the ESD protection.
Enumeration and flashing with U3 removed verify the bypassed USB data path and do not verify restored ESD protection.
